recent_posts.title: Godot usage and engine growth – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot Engine shares growth metrics across multiple dimensions including engine downloads (approaching 2 million per release), community size (doubled in recent years), Steam game releases (showing exponential growth), game jam participation (rising share in Global Game Jam and GMTK), and donation fund performance. Key findings: patch releases cannibalize stable downloads as expected, Godot games on Steam are growing exponentially, game jam usage is climbing toward 50%, but monthly donations have remained relatively flat despite user growth. The post also notes data limitations including no built-in telemetry, gaps in Discord tracking, and underrepresentation of non-Western communities like China.

recent_posts.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.7 beta 1 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot 4.7 has reached its first beta milestone with 1265 fixes from 309 contributors since 4.6-stable. Key highlights include full HDR output support across Windows, macOS, Linux, and BSD; Vulkan raytracing groundwork; nearest-neighbor 3D viewport scaling for pixel-art games; rectangular area light sources (AreaLight3D); a new DrawableTexture API; and inline shader previews in the text editor. Editor improvements are extensive: 3D vertex snapping, Path3D collider snapping, a new Scene Paint tool for 2D, revamped asset store UI, MeshLibrary bottom editor, monospaced fonts for code symbols, and selective export template downloads. Physics gains configurable one-way collision directions for CollisionShape2D. Input adds a built-in VirtualJoystick node for touchscreens. Android gets picture-in-picture support and portrait mode in the script editor. Several breaking changes are noted, including Jolt Physics SoftBody3D defaults and particle angular velocity fixes.

recent_posts.title: HDR output arrives in Godot 4.7 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot 4.7 introduces HDR output support for Windows, macOS, iOS, visionOS, and Linux (Wayland only). The feature allows games to display greater detail in bright areas rather than simply boosting brightness. It requires the Forward+ or Mobile renderer and specific graphics APIs (Direct3D 12 on Windows, Metal or Vulkan on Apple platforms, Vulkan on Linux). Enabling it is as simple as toggling a project setting, though developers are encouraged to expose HDR calibration options to players. The implementation involved significant rework of tonemapping, glow, and debanding systems to ensure HDR-awareness across Godot's rendering pipeline.

recent_posts.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.7 dev 5 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot 4.7 dev 5 snapshot is out, packed with last-minute contributions ahead of feature freeze. Key highlights include: a revamped asset store ported to a new API with improved UI and metadata display; a new export template dialog that allows downloading individual platform templates instead of bulk packages; em-based image scaling in RichTextLabel; inline shader previews in the text shader editor; and a new rectangular area light source (AreaLight3D) for 3D rendering. Additional improvements cover audio bus UI revamp, Android embedded window support, Wayland touch input, raytracing pipeline refactoring, and more. 71 contributors submitted 135 fixes in this snapshot.

recent_posts.title: Godot Mobile update — April 2026 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: The Godot Foundation's mobile team shares progress on improving Godot's mobile capabilities across Android and iOS. Key updates include: new and maintained ecosystem plugins for Google Play Billing, Google Play Games Services, and Apple StoreKit 2 to support in-app purchases and store features; GPU driver compatibility fixes that reduced crash rates from ~4% to under 1% in real shipped games; native Android debug symbols and Android instrumented test support for automated device testing; Perfetto and Instruments profiler integration; and Android device mirroring directly from the editor. Future work will focus on rendering, performance, testing infrastructure, and plugin coverage.

recent_posts.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.7 dev 4 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot 4.7 dev 4 snapshot is now available with 188 fixes from 88 contributors. Key highlights include nearest-neighbor scaling for 3D viewports (benefiting pixel-art and low-resolution games), a new `custom_maximum_size` property for GUI Control nodes, improved drag-and-drop behavior in Tree nodes with a visual indicator, and increased inspector space for array properties. Additional changes cover TileSet editor rework, 3D ruler vector components, Visual Profiler folding, Android Java interface support from GDScript, Windows OneCore TTS and emoji picker support, and various particle bug fixes. This is a pre-release build intended for testing ahead of feature freeze.

recent_posts.title: Godot Showcase – Xogot: Godot for iPad & iPhone – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Xogot is a native iOS port of the Godot game engine editor for iPad and iPhone, developed by Xibbon and led by Miguel de Icaza (creator of GNOME, Mono, and Xamarin). The project required solving major technical challenges including iPadOS's single-process constraint (solved by virtualizing all global variables to run multiple Godot instances simultaneously), rebuilding nearly the entire UI in SwiftUI to meet Apple's touch-first design standards (44pt minimum tap targets), and embedding Godot within a native iOS shell. Key limitations include no support for native third-party plugins or .NET code due to Apple's security model. Xibbon also contributed LibGodot upstream, enabling Godot to be embedded in other applications. Future plans include Xogot Connect (an open-source add-on for desktop developers to run/debug on iOS devices) and eventual support for Apple Vision Pro.

recent_posts.title: Maintenance release: Godot 4.6.2 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot 4.6.2 is a maintenance release with 122 fixes from 61 contributors. Key fixes include animation editor improvements, core RingBuffer bugs, rendering issues (viewport debanding, canvas renderer memory reads, tangent decoding), Jolt Physics accuracy improvements, platform-specific fixes for Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Wayland, and several editor usability fixes. No known incompatibilities with 4.6.1 exist, and all users are encouraged to upgrade.

recent_posts.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.7 dev 3 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot 4.7 dev 3 is out with 297 fixes from 113 contributors. Key highlights include transform offset properties for Control nodes enabling CSS-like visual transforms without breaking container layout, a search bar for PopupMenu nodes, vertex snapping in the 3D editor, improved remote scene tree with class names instead of Object IDs, a new dedicated MeshLibrary editor for GridMap users, Android picture-in-picture support, portrait mode in the Android script editor, and HDR output support on Linux via Wayland. Additional improvements cover animation optimizations, thread-safety for Object signals, rendering fast paths, and various editor UX improvements.

recent_posts.title: Release candidate: Godot 4.6.2 RC 2 – Godot Engine
recent_posts.summary: Godot Engine has released the second Release Candidate for version 4.6.2, incorporating 29 improvements from 25 contributors since RC1. The changes are primarily regression fixes spanning 3D editor, animation, GUI, rendering, platform-specific issues (macOS, iOS, Windows, Android), build system updates, and third-party library updates (libpng 1.6.55, access-kit 0.21.2). Both Standard and .NET builds are available for testing.

top_posts.title: Godot 4.6 focuses on polish and workflow improvements
top_posts.summary: Godot 4.6 focuses on polish and quality-of-life improvements after three years of maturation. With over 1,200 Steam releases in 2025 and 500 weekly itch.io games, the engine is now fully capable but needed workflow refinements. This release addresses minor roadblocks, papercuts, and bugs to improve the development experience. Nearly 400 contributors authored 2,001 commits for this update.

top_posts.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.3 dev 6
top_posts.summary: Godot 4.3 dev 6 is the last dev snapshot before entering the beta phase. It is feature-packed with 650 commits and includes important bug fixes and improvements in various engine areas. Highlights include the implementation of fixed timestep for 2D physics interpolation, the exposure of TileMap layers as individual nodes, the use of base64 encoding for PackedByteArray serialization, and the addition of automatic checking for engine updates.

top_posts.title: Web Export in 4.3
top_posts.summary: Godot 4.3 promises improved Web exports with fixes for single-threaded exports and introduces sample playback for better audio quality. It also allows for easy COOP-COEP PWA for threaded builds.

top_posts.title: Design of the Skeleton Modifier 3D
top_posts.summary: Godot 4.3 introduces the SkeletonModifier3D node to improve bone animation by handling it outside the AnimationMixer and eliminating the limitations of the previous pose override system. This new design ensures a consistent processing order, making complex scene management easier. Users can create custom SkeletonModifier3D nodes for specific needs and use signals to retrieve modified pose values. Future versions will include additional built-in SkeletonModifier3D nodes like IK and constraints.
